subject: Next steps & budget-owner intro — Redwood demo follow-up (Aurora Tech)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Park <samantha.park@auroratech.com>, Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@auroratech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up + next steps after today's demo

Hi Samantha / Diego,

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps: 

Summary of call:
- Use case: Aurora wants to reduce latency and inference cost for customer-facing summarization pipeline while preserving answer quality.
- Current infra: in-house endpoints on A100s, struggling with tail latency at peak.
- Success criteria: 95th pct latency < 300ms, cost < $X/token (TBD), and SOC2-compliant ops.

Open items we agreed to:
1) Identify the economic buyer / budget owner who will sign off on reserved capacity.
2) Procurement/security evidence checklist to start (SOC2, data flow diagram, encryption).
3) Canonical production workload sample + P95 latency target for sizing.

Proposed next steps:
- I will put together a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that outlines milestones and responsibilities.
- Can you introduce me to the person who owns the budget (or confirm whether Diego is the budget owner)?
- Please loop in procurement/security contacts so we can start the compliance exchange.

I'll attach the MAP and a preliminary pricing sheet to give ballpark numbers for dedicated capacity and hosted options. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute procurement call next week.

Thanks again — I'll standby for the intro.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: mutual_action_plan.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Attachment: redwood_pricing_sheet.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Samantha Park <samantha.park@auroratech.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@auroratech.com>, procurement@auroratech.com
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps after today's demo

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the recap and the demo — helpful. A few notes:

- Diego is the VP of Engineering and will influence the technical and budget direction, but final sign-off sits with our Head of Cloud Operations, Maria Chen (I can introduce).
- I've cc'd our procurement team (procurement@auroratech.com) so they can start the compliance checklist.
- Please send a one-pager that calls out: pricing ranges for hosted vs dedicated, expected latency improvements, and what evidence we can provide for SOC2/KMS.

Procurement asked for a MAP and any standard contract templates you typically use. If you can include a trimmed-down version of the MAP and a pricing band, we can route internally.

We can do a procurement call next Thurs if that works.

Thanks,
Samantha
Senior Product Manager
Aurora Tech

Hi Samantha / Maria / procurement team,

Attaching a concise Mutual Action Plan that lays out milestones, owners, and timing. Also attached is a preliminary pricing sheet showing hosted API rates, dedicated reserved capacity monthly ranges, and an example TCO comparison for a 6-month pilot.

Key ask: could Maria or Samantha confirm who will own the budget conversation? If Maria is the owner, it'd be great to schedule a 20-min budget alignment to confirm runway and procurement timing. If someone else owns the budget, could you please introduce them to me?

- Week 1: Kickoff procurement call (compliance doc exchange).
- Week 2: Pilot provisioning + sample workload run (we provide baseline scoring).
- Week 4: Pilot review and capacity proposal.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.pdf, redwood_pricing_sheet.xlsx

Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:25:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Aurora Tech — pricing guidance & discount request (DEAL-2027-AT-009)

Marissa / Vivek,

Quick internal note after Samantha looped in procurement and Maria:
- They need a MAP + pricing band to route internally (sent).
- Maria Chen is likely the budget owner; Samantha asked to confirm — waiting on intro.

Ask for you: can we approve a pilot discount structure? Proposal: 3-month pilot at 40% off list for dedicated reserved capacity (committed 4 GPUs) with a markup for overage. I'd also like a one-time onboarding credit to cover integration work.

If possible please confirm redlines we should expect from procurement (SLA, data residency, indemnity language) and whether we want legal to pre-approve a pilot amendment.

I'll follow up as soon as Maria introduces herself.

Thanks,
Alex
